comparator.name: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS. Years 1 and 2 are fixed 60-ECTS sequences in cognitive science, programming, mathematics, statistics, AI, machine learning, neuroscience, autonomous systems and research. Year 3 combines the official first-listed 30-ECTS Exchange/Study Abroad mobility option with 18 ECTS of Hybrid Intelligence, Computational Linguistics and Ethics of AI and a 12-ECTS CSAI thesis. The mobility option is retained as genuine open programme space rather than populated with invented courses.

components.name: Exchange/Study Abroad

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two independently generator-backed and feasible organising directions: computational AI and autonomous systems; and cognitive, language and responsible human-centred AI. Each produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-ECTS distinctness floor, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce programming, computational problem solving, data structures and debugging.
Both advance programming through software design, development practice, testing and maintainability.
Both deepen introductory AI through intelligent decision-making under uncertainty and constraints.
Both develop algorithms and data structures with attention to design and performance.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Introduction to AI 1 component.
No selected UCR course provides a sufficiently direct one-to-one counterpart to the full Multi-Agent Systems component.
Both introduce core machine-learning methods including regression, resampling, trees and support-vector approaches.
Both cover neural networks and deep-learning methods for images, language and generative AI.
Both study autonomous embodied systems; UCR focuses on robotics, sensing, kinematics and control.
Both establish mathematical methods used in quantitative and computational study; UCR also covers linear algebra and differential equations.
Both develop linear spaces, vectors, matrices and their computational applications.
Both develop formal and discrete reasoning for computational problem solving and artificial intelligence.
Both provide advanced probability and statistical modelling beyond the introductory level.
Both teach statistical inference and hands-on analysis of empirical data.
Both introduce cognition, behaviour and relationships between mental processes and brain systems.

notes.text: Tilburg’s Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence bachelor provides a tightly integrated 150-ECTS specialist sequence plus a 30-ECTS mobility window, with continuous programming, mathematics, AI, cognitive science, machine learning, neuroscience, autonomous systems, computational linguistics and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can assemble strong AI pathways across these fields, but it does not reproduce the same prescribed specialist progression or dedicated laboratory infrastructure.

UCR does not provide direct equivalents for Tilburg’s complete introductory AI sequence, Multi-Agent Systems, dedicated Human-Computer Interaction course, Hybrid Intelligence course or 12-ECTS CSAI thesis. Those gaps remain explicit rather than being filled with weak substitutes.
